subjects.displayTitle: Goodly deeds: when conviction becomes a gift to the world
subjects.introduction: Someone is hungry and cold, and our certainty that generosity is a virtue feeds no one. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá begins there, with the plain fact that knowledge is not enough, and Bahá’u’lláh presses the point: deeds are the test of words, and words without them cannot quench a single thirst. An unbeliever who does good is judged better than a professing believer whose conduct betrays him, and a Bahá’í is to be known by deeds rather than by name. Yet action is never cut loose from the inner life. A deed set as a snare to win reward loses its life; a charity performed for admiration spoils in the giving; the act done purely, however small, outweighs a mountain in the mirror of God’s knowledge and leaves a fragrance that never fades. Faith, in the Epistle of James, faces the same brother or sister in need of warmth and food, and is asked what it has actually supplied. The road runs on from here into the old quarrel between words and deeds, into service to others, and into the quiet authority of example.
subjects.arc: Begin with concrete human need and the test of conduct; explore faith, knowledge and intention; follow deeds into service, teaching and community life; close with enduring fruit and a practical invitation to participation.

order.why: State deeds as the test of words.
shortened: O people! Words must be supported by deeds, for deeds are the true test of words. Without the former, the latter can never quench the thirst of the yearning soul, nor unlock the portals of vision before the eyes of the blind.

order.why: Open with the hungry and cold person whom knowledge alone cannot help.
shortened: Knowledge is not enough. We hope by the Love of God we shall put it into practice. A spiritual universal force is needed for this. Meetings are good for engendering spiritual force. To know that to reach a state of perfection is possible is good, to march forward on the path is better. We know that to help the poor and to be merciful is good and pleases God, but knowledge alone does not feed the starving man, nor can the poor be warmed by knowledge or words, in the bitter winter.

order.why: Imagine actions as mirrors of what grows in the heart.
Give a small act the scale of a mountain or sea.
shortened: An act, however infinitesimal, is, when viewed in the mirror of the knowledge of God, mightier than a mountain. Every drop proffered in His path is as the sea in that mirror.

order.why: Notice benefit returning to both doer and recipient.
shortened: And whatsoever virtuous deeds have been revealed in the Holy Tablets from the Divine Pen - the benefit thereof shall return both to the doer and to the one for whom it was done.

order.why: Ask how love finds an object, instrument and motive.
shortened: Love manifests its reality in deeds, not only in words -- these alone are without effect. In order that love may manifest its power there must be an object, an instrument, a motive.

order.why: Challenge a reliance on religious profession without good conduct.
shortened: Certainly, a non-believer who performs good deeds is better than one who claims love and faith but whose deeds reveal satanic temptations. However, perfection is achieved when deeds and faith are combined, and the person of good conduct strives to spread the unity of the human world and promote peace and oneness among the nations and peoples of the world.

order.why: Bring divine acceptance and freedom from bargaining into the opening inquiry.
shortened: Make not your deeds as snares wherewith to entrap the object of your aspiration, and deprive not yourselves of this Ultimate Objective for which have ever yearned all such as have drawn nigh unto God. Say: The very life of all deeds is My good pleasure, and all things depend upon Mine acceptance.
All that are on earth shall pass away, while good deeds alone shall endure; to the truth of My words God doth Himself bear witness.

order.why: Join consistency of speech and deed with reciprocity.
Let righteous deeds testify to words.
Read the three Hidden Words passages through purity and practical guidance.
shortened: Holy words and pure and goodly deeds ascend unto the heaven of celestial glory. Strive that your deeds may be cleansed from the dust of self and hypocrisy and find favor at the court of glory; for ere long the assayers of mankind shall, in the holy presence of the Adored One, accept naught but absolute virtue and deeds of stainless purity.

Guidance hath ever been given by words, and now it is given by deeds. Every one must show forth deeds that are pure and holy, for words are the property of all alike, whereas such deeds as these belong only to Our loved ones. Strive then with heart and soul to distinguish yourselves by your deeds.

order.why: Ask what signs make spiritual development perceptible.
shortened: If a man is not characterized by these excellent qualities, it is certain that he has never attained to so much as a drop out of the fathomless river of the waters of life that flows through the teachings of the Holy Books, nor caught the faintest breath of the fragrant breezes that blow from the gardens of God; for nothing on earth can be demonstrated by words alone, and every level of existence is known by its signs and symbols, and every degree in man's development has its identifying mark.

order.why: Distinguish recognizing a good from attaining or producing it.
Follow thought toward expression in action.
Keep the reported challenge to excessive talk.
shortened: The world is wrong, just because people talk too much and do not carry out their ideals. If action took the place of words, the world would change very soon.

order.why: Preserve the forceful definition of faith in its source wording.
shortened:
The essence of faith is fewness of words and abundance
of deeds; he whose words exceed his deeds, know verily his
death is better than his life.

order.why: Retain the severe contrast between speaking and practicing.
Read inconsistency beside the source’s religious example.
Question acceptance that coexists with pride or treachery.
shortened: Mere acceptance of the Cause and acknowledgment of the truth is not and hath never been sufficient, even as all people today make such claims, yet the Tongue of Grandeur beareth witness to their lies, calumnies, pride, heedlessness and treachery.

order.why: Keep the warning about recognition contradicted by deeds.
shortened: How many souls there are who claim to have turned to Him and recognized Him, yet in their deeds and actions they are found wanting.

order.why: Connect inward belief with outward evidence.
shortened: O thou who art attracted by the divine fragrances wafting from the gardens of knowledge! The stages of spiritual recognition, certitude, faith and assurance require proofs and evidence, signs and testimonies. The inward without the outward is deficient, and belief without deeds is void.

order.why: Consider how concealed faith becomes visible through sincerity.
shortened: O thou who art firm and steadfast! Faith pertains to the heart and soul, and this is a hidden and concealed matter. However, its proof lies in deeds and conduct. If one's way and behavior demonstrate sincerity, then it is established and confirmed.

order.why: Read deeds as mirrors revealing the doer.
Join the mirror image with truthfulness and trustworthiness.
State conduct as the location of human quality.
shortened: The quality of man lies in his conduct and deeds.

order.why: Keep the concise connection between actions and station.
Consider behavior as a standard of discernment.
shortened: This is the standard - look ye at every soul according to their deeds and behavior, that the fruit of existence may become manifest and the banner of guidance may wave through the holy fragrances.

order.why: Read that standard through the fruits of existence.
Keep the reported interpretation of knowing a tree by its fruits.
shortened: Christ said, 'You will know them by their fruits,' that is, by their deeds. If a believer shows forth divine qualities, we know the true Faith is in his heart. If we do not find evidence of these qualities, if he is selfish or wicked, he has not the true kind of Faith.

order.why: Retain the separate reported Gospel allusion.
shortened: The Baha'is must be known by their deeds. That is why His Holiness the Christ says: ye shall know the trees by their fruits.

order.why: Read the fruitless-tree saying in its attributed form.
Keep the brief tree comparison in its own source.
Join fruitfulness with the present call to action.
Preserve the concise warning against fruitlessness.
shortened: In truth, a person without deeds has been and is fruitless.

order.why: Keep the deeds and conditions named as fruit.
Imagine a good deed as a growing sapling.
Offer the fruits with joy and wisdom to others.
shortened: Now is the time for fruits and leaves, and the fruits of the divine tree have ever been and are goodly deeds and praiseworthy character. Withhold not these fruits from the heedless. Show them forth with spirit and joy, with wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Read promised fruits and trees through their educational purpose.
shortened: This is why God, exalted be His glory, hath mentioned in His Perspicuous Book, which distinguisheth between truth and falsehood, the mention of paradise and fruits and trees. And this matter, in one respect, is purely for the education of creation, that they might act virtuously and through this blessed deed attain unto lofty stations.

order.why: Explore a Bahá’í identity expressed in the whole of life.
shortened: They should justify their claim to be Baha'is by deeds and not by name. He is a true Baha'i who strives by day and by night to progress and advance along the path of human endeavour, whose most cherished desire is so to live and act as to enrich and illuminate the world, whose source of inspiration is the essence of divine virtue, whose aim in life is so to conduct himself as to be the cause of infinite progress.

For in this holy Dispensation, the crowning glory of bygone ages and cycles, true faith is no mere acknowledgement of the unity of God, but rather the living of a life that will manifest all the perfections and virtues implied in such belief.

order.why: Follow patient active service into civilization, science and arts.
shortened: Our actions will help on the world, will spread civilization, will help the progress of science, and cause the arts to develop. Without action nothing in the material world can be accomplished, neither can words unaided advance a man in the spiritual Kingdom. It is not through lip-service only that the elect of God have attained to holiness, but by patient lives of active service they have brought light into the world.

order.why: Keep the reported appeal to motiveless love and corresponding faith and action.
shortened: Be a Baha'i in reality and not in word. Be detached, be spiritual, love thy fellowmen with a motiveless love. Let thy mind be a palace of universal ideals, and thy heart the casket of the jewels of sympathy and affection. Give and not [sic] take. Be generous in thought, in act and in feeling. Let thy faith and action correspond with each other.

order.why: Preserve the brief reported distinction concerning lived faith.
Read the reported contrast of mere acceptance and bettering conditions.
shortened: But in this day the question is far more important. Faith does not consist in belief, it consists in deeds. It is not sufficient to believe in Baha'u'llah and to say, "I am of the people of El-Abha"; we must act in accordance with the teachings of Baha'u'llah, who commands us to become centers of divine attraction, so that the attributes of God may emanate from us, that we may become wise and well intentioned to all the peoples of the earth in order to better the condition of all.

order.why: Retain the separate reported definition of belief through qualities and acts.
Keep the extended reported appeal with its source omission.
shortened: Faith means Deeds and in turn Deeds mean Faith. If a Baha'i is confirmed in Deeds, he is accepted. His faith in and acknowledgement of the station of Baha'u'llah do not bring him in the rank of the people of the Kingdom of Abha.
In short he must demonstrate his love for all the people through every loving means.

Just as light appear through an illumined lamp, likewise these deeds must appear from a person who calls himself a Baha'i; otherwise one does not become a Baha'i by merely acknowledging the station of Baha'u'llah...

order.why: Read concrete services as the proof of faith.
shortened: Faith is not only in words. Such services are the proof of faith.

order.why: Bring the standard to an address to two women.
shortened: O ye two well-loved handmaids of God! Whatever a man's tongue speaketh, that let him prove by his deeds. If he claimeth to be a believer, then let him act in accordance with the precepts of the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Keep the reported criterion of relationship through example.
Find wonder in sustained obedience amid a storm.
Read the reported call to embody teachings.
shortened: It is my hope that all the friends will arise in the service of the Cause; that they will live in accord with the Teachings of Baha'u'llah and the contents of my addresses; so that these Teachings may not become like Bible, unfulfilled.
All the friends must become the living embodiments of these Teachings; otherwise they will not avail.

order.why: Attend to the reported gap between great teachings and their practice.
Read the scriptural connection of righteous work and hope for divine presence.
Introduce the call for deeds to proceed from knowledge.
Keep the answer about the fruit and completeness of deeds.
Read the account joining knowledge, love and sincere motive.
shortened: Briefly, good deeds become perfect and complete only after the knowledge of God has been acquired, the love of God has been manifested, and spiritual attractions and goodly motives have been attained.  Otherwise, though good deeds be praiseworthy, if they do not spring from the knowledge of God, from the love of God, and from a sincere intention, they will be imperfect.

order.why: Preserve the reported joining of knowledge, action and recognition.
Connect divine unity with righteous deeds.
shortened: There are those who believe that the cause of salvation is none other than a confession of Divine Unity. There are those who say: "This is not sufficient. Belief in Divine Unity must be combined with righteous deeds as prescribed by the All-Merciful."

order.why: Read recognition and the Book as guides to action.
shortened: After recognition of the Manifestation of Divine Revelation and the Dawning-Place of the Divine Inspiration, Who is the Sovereign of beliefs, all must act according to that which hath been sent down in the Book, for it is the Sovereign of deeds.

order.why: Consider nearness and acceptance within the passage’s account of unity.
shortened: O Rida! This Wronged One has ever remembered His loved ones and counselled all to that which brings them nearer to God. Such nearness cannot be attained except through goodly deeds and praiseworthy conduct. Deeds and their acceptance are, in the first instance and highest station, dependent upon the divine unity.

order.why: Keep the warning that deeds can themselves obstruct the ultimate aim.
Preserve the reported ideal of inward and outward correspondence with its source lacuna.
shortened: Blessed is the soul whose outward life is the same as its inward life; whose Lord has guided it, removed its veil, and honoured it with the cup (of consolation) mixed with camphor, to... [incomplete]

order.why: Imagine intention and action becoming one.
shortened: Blessed is the soul between whose intention and deed no difference is seen - whose intention is the very deed and whose deed is the very intention. And this is the station of the depths of the sea of oneness that was mentioned before.

order.why: Introduce the cited tradition on motives.
shortened: O you who are yearning for the threshold of the Intended One!
In the previous Dispensation, there is a tradition which states: "Deeds are judged by their motives, and for every person is what they have intended."

order.why: Keep the reported distinction between good intention and mixed motives in action.
shortened: This means that when a man has a good intention, that is, cherishes the desire in his heart for a righteous act, it is impossible that such an intention by anything but pure. whereas, in acting, it is possible that selfish reasons may have prompted it. For instance, it is possible that a man performs a good deed with a view to personal interst; such a good deed done is not separated from hypocrisy and insincerity. But when a man cherishes a good intention, it is impossible that it be prompted by any prejudice or be intended for anything but good.

order.why: Examine the temptation to seek admiration through charity.
Read the reported fragrance enjoyed without seeking applause.
shortened: "The good deeds of man are like unto the sweet fragrances emanated from the musk. They perfume the nostrils of every one more especially the doer. As his deeds have been performed with no reference to the applause and commendation of men he enjoys them more than any one else.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s farewell appeal to pure motives and deeds.
shortened: The days when idle worship was deemed sufficient are ended. The time is come when naught but the purest motive, supported by deeds of stainless purity, can ascend to the throne of the Most High and be acceptable unto Him.

order.why: Name sincere intention and charity as nourishment.
shortened: The first food is the love of God. The second food is attraction to the breaths of the Holy Spirit. The third food is unity and harmony among all the divine friends. The fourth food is charitable deeds and sincere intentions. The fifth food is truthfulness and trustworthiness and kindness and purity of intention and service to all humanity.

order.why: Retain the counsel to act purely for God.
shortened: Hold thou fast unto that which beseemeth thee throughout the Kingdom of earth and heaven, and that is a deed which is performed purely for the sake of God by His servants.

order.why: Read the Bab’s call to abundant deeds for God.
shortened: Fear ye the All-Merciful, O servants, and perform good deeds abundantly for the sake of God, the True One.

order.why: Connect pure words and deeds with detachment.
shortened: Say: O people! Nothing ascendeth unto God save pure words and goodly deeds, and He loveth those who are detached. Aid ye God through your deeds, and be not of those who are veiled.

order.why: Keep the image of purity as a sweet savor.
shortened: We verily behold your actions. If We perceive from them the sweet smelling savor of purity and holiness, We will most certainly bless you.

order.why: Join action with love and the companionship of true counselors.
Read the virtues whose practice could prevent discord.
Give truthfulness, courtesy, forbearance and justice concrete prominence.
shortened: Say: Let truthfulness and courtesy be your adorning. Suffer not yourselves to be deprived of the robe of forbearance and justice, that the sweet savors of holiness may be wafted from your hearts upon all created things. Say: Beware, O people of Bahá, lest ye walk in the ways of them whose words differ from their deeds.

Let your acts be a guide unto all mankind, for the professions of most men, be they high or low, differ from their conduct. It is through your deeds that ye can distinguish yourselves from others. Through them the brightness of your light can be shed upon the whole earth.

order.why: Connect the counsels to love, kindness and rest.
shortened: O Rida, We counsel you in all conditions to fear God, to goodly deeds, and to that which causes the manifestation of love and kindness. What does the Book say? That which benefits you. What has God commanded? That which brings salvation and bestows rest.

order.why: Name trustworthiness and truthfulness as present tasks.
shortened: This is the Day for pure deeds. God willing, the friends of Truth must appear among the servants with perfect trustworthiness, truthfulness and praiseworthy character.

order.why: Make love across religions and races visible through action.
shortened: Love ye all religions and all races with a love that is true and sincere and show that love through deeds and not through the tongue; for the latter hath no importance, as the majority of men are, in speech, well-wishers, while action is the best.

order.why: Keep the call to manifest universal love.
Read the reported relation of service, nearness and human satisfaction.
Join those already working for the poor and vulnerable in the reported reply.
shortened: When asked by an American friend: "Which is the best way to spread the teaching?" he said:
"By deeds. This way is open to all, and deeds are understood by all. Join yourselves to those who work for the poor, the weak and the unfortunate; this is greatly to be commended.

order.why: Attend to the happiness and gratitude of other people.
shortened: Always strive to make hearts grateful and become the cause of happiness, contentment, gratitude and success for souls who have turned to God, especially those who deserve respect.

order.why: Keep appreciation of particular services.
Read the reported test of an idea through kind relationships.
shortened: The only test of its truth lies in the influence this conception has upon our lives; if it makes us kind and loving in our relations with our fellow-men, we may know it is a true one.

order.why: Preserve the reported recognition of good deeds across religions.
shortened: "The most important thing is deeds. Good deeds are accepted by all nations and religions.

order.why: Apply correspondence between teaching and action to a gathering.
shortened: The mercifulness of every gathering-place is to correspond the deeds, actions and behaviour in accord with the Teachings of God.

order.why: Read spiritual education through the pursuit of praiseworthy actions.
Imagine a shared palace built from philanthropic deeds.
shortened: Praiseworthy deeds and philanthropic actions are the materials with which the palace is built. Vices and the degeneracy of morality are the axes with which the very foundation of this eternal palace laid by the hand of God is uprooted.

order.why: Keep the original short call for execution and effect.
Let the brush of deeds paint ideals into existence.
Read the reported requirement that spiritual life give life.
shortened: That which is truly spiritual must light the path to God, and must result in deeds. We cannot believe the call to be spiritual when there is no result. Spirit is reality, and when the spirit in each of us seeks to join itself with the Great Reality, it must in turn give life.

order.why: Retain the separate reported account of actions as fruits of faith.
shortened: The real thing is faith, first of all. Actions and deeds are the fruits of faith. The fulfillment of salvation and safety is the faith.

order.why: Keep fasting and prayer beside the fruit-bearing image.
shortened: Hold fast to fasting and prayer. A person without deeds is, according to Christ, like a tree without fruit, and a fruitless tree hath ever been and will ever be fit for the fire."

order.why: Connect outward deeds with hope, fasting and prayer.
shortened: The Book of God, which distinguisheth between truth and falsehood, ever calleth unto the people of divine unity, saying: "Act, O My loved ones, according to that which ye have been commanded." For the station of hope is manifested through outward deeds, and fasting and prayer are as the sun and moon in the heaven of divine ordinances.

order.why: Read the Hidden Words with the intention of practicing them.
shortened: O honored Qabil! We must recite the Persian and Arabic Hidden Words day and night, and implore and supplicate that we may act according to these divine counsels. These sacred words were revealed for action, not just for hearing.

order.why: Keep the particular reported scene urging action during prayer in its source setting.
shortened: While he was engaged in prayer she came and began to talk with him most vehemently that this is the day of work, action. Get up and do something. This day of prayer is not now.

order.why: Preserve the reported comparison of Christian profession and conduct with its qualification.
Make the teacher’s conduct attest the utterance.
shortened: As to the fundamentals of teaching the Faith: know thou that delivering the Message can be accomplished only through goodly deeds and spiritual attributes, an utterance that is crystal clear and the happiness reflected from the face of that one who is expounding the Teachings. It is essential that the deeds of the teacher should attest the truth of his words.

order.why: Read the reported need to implement before influencing others.
shortened: The Baha'is themselves must first be implementers of the teachings so that they may have effect on others. How can one who has not found existence from the Giver of existence give existence to others?

order.why: Keep the reported explanation of teachings through purity and behavior.
Follow the influence of deeds toward reform, peace and concord.
shortened: The influence of deeds is more potent than the influence of words. Goodly deeds and spiritual qualities are each a herald of truth amongst the servants. The triumph of God's Cause dependeth upon these hosts. Perchance souls may arise for the sake of God and deliver the servants from the oppression of the ravenous ones of the earth, that corruption may be transformed into reformation, war into peace, and discord into concord.

order.why: Read the liberating deed and the hosts of character together.
shortened: One pure deed shall transcend the heavens; it shall loose the bound wing and restore departed strength.

Say: O people of God! The Helper and Succourer and the hosts of God are, in the Scriptures and Tablets, manifest and evident as the sun. These hosts have ever been and shall remain goodly deeds and praiseworthy character. Whosoever today rendereth assistance through the hosts of righteous deeds and character, and ariseth to serve for God and in the path of God, assuredly shall his traces become manifest and evident in all regions.

order.why: Understand the passage’s weapon as good words, deeds and character.
shortened: In these days, in one of the Tablets, this exalted word hath flowed from the Most Exalted Pen -- glorified be His utterance: "At all times, hold fast to that which will cause the exaltation of the Word of God. Goodly deeds and a praiseworthy character are the hosts of God in this supreme Revelation, and likewise are blessed and goodly words. These hosts attract hearts and unlock the gates of cities. This weapon is sharper than the weapons of the world."

order.why: Keep the comparison of deeds with swords as a statement of moral influence.
Retain the contrast with the power of worldly armies.
shortened: By the Sun of Truth! The influence of pure deeds and praiseworthy character is greater and mightier than the influence of the ranks and hosts on high. Its power and might cannot be weakened by the power of the world's armies.

order.why: Join wisdom and utterance to the standards of sanctity and justice.
Read the conquering of hearts through these named hosts.
shortened: O friends! We counsel all to that which is the cause of the exaltation of the Word of God. The hosts which have been and shall forever be victorious and triumphant are goodly deeds and praiseworthy character. Blessed are they who with these hosts have conquered the citadels of hearts.

order.why: Keep the definition of earthly hosts as conduct and deeds.
shortened: Say: Hold fast unto deeds and unto that which We have revealed concerning conduct, then know ye that these are God's hosts on earth. He in Whose possession is the Mother Book doth testify to this. Aid ye your Lord through goodly character - through this His Cause is exalted in all regions.

order.why: Retain the concise account of divine assistance.
shortened: Divine assistance has been and ever will be through goodly deeds and praiseworthy character.

order.why: Preserve the remembered emphasis on deeds as promoters of the Cause.
shortened: Repeatedly have such words been heard from the tongue of Him Who revealeth the verses. He would say that today righteous deeds and praiseworthy character are the promoters of the Cause of God. It is hoped that all shall be assisted to achieve that which is acceptable in the presence of God.

order.why: Join acting with comprehending in the stated assistance.
Follow the guiding fragrance of an act performed for God.
Read assistance beside relinquishing desire.
shortened: In truth I say, pure deeds and praiseworthy character have been and continue to be the helpers of God's Cause in this Most Great Revelation. Blessed is he who renounceth his desires and holdeth fast unto the fear of God. He is assuredly among those who are nigh unto God in My perspicuous Book.

order.why: Keep the appeal to steadfast souls to assist through character.
shortened: Those steadfast souls who have quaffed from the crimson cup the Kawthar of immortality must assist the Cause of God through goodly deeds and praiseworthy character.

order.why: Retain the direct call to aid the All-Merciful through deeds.
shortened: O people of Baha! Aid ye the All-Merciful through deeds and virtuous character. This is what We commanded you before and in this glorious Tablet.

order.why: Keep the recurring counsel in the Tablets.
Read the stated basis of triumph.
shortened: The triumph of God's Cause hath ever been and shall continue to be through goodly deeds and praiseworthy and pleasing character.

order.why: Define service through praiseworthy human actions.
Consider deeds as promoters in themselves.
shortened: Goodly deeds are in themselves promoters of God's Cause and have ever been so. Blessed is he who acteth according to that which hath been commanded by God, and woe unto the heedless.

order.why: Keep the worldwide address to the loved ones.
Set praiseworthy character beside the condemnation of contention.
shortened: Corruption, conflict and contention have ever been and shall ever be condemned. That which today is the cause of the exaltation of man's station are goodly deeds and praiseworthy character. Blessed are they that act, and woe unto them that neglect.

order.why: Read deeds as a way of counseling others.
Retain the repeated account of victory through character.
Explore the relation between requested service and conduct.
shortened: As for what thou didst desire concerning service, know that it dependeth upon goodly deeds and praiseworthy character. By Him Who holdeth my soul in His hands! Deeds are more potent than words. It behooveth the people of unity to counsel others through their deeds and their character.

order.why: Consider the account of one deed’s far-reaching influence.
shortened: Through one goodly deed that appeared from him, an entire kingdom--from its king and ministers and princes and others--became illumined with the lights of faith. Now consider what power, might and influence a single deed hath wrought and manifested.

order.why: Let manners and conduct point toward their Source.
Read the righteous deed as itself a teacher.
shortened: I swear by the peerless Pearl of the ocean of utterance that a righteous deed is, in itself, a teacher of God's Cause. Exert yourselves to act in accordance with what hath been sent down from the Most Exalted Pen in the Book.

order.why: Connect remembrance and joy with the call to assist.
shortened: Rejoice ye in My remembrance of you, then assist your Lord through goodly character and deeds. Thus doth command you the perspicuous Book that speaketh with truth between the heavens and the earth and summoneth all unto God, the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Preserve the personal address emphasizing character.
shortened: O Zayn'l-Abidin! Know thou with absolute certitude that goodly deeds and praiseworthy character have ever been and shall ever be the cause of the exaltation of the Word of God.

order.why: Follow the fragrance that attracts souls.
shortened: Today all must act according to that which God hath commanded, so that the fragrance of pure deeds may attract souls to the direction of the Lord of the Beginning and the End.

order.why: Keep the direct appeal to aid through deeds.
shortened: Ye must aid the Cause of God through goodly deeds and praiseworthy character.

order.why: Retain the concise statement concerning victory.
shortened: Victory has been and ever will be through the hosts of deeds and character.

order.why: Read the inclusive command to maidservants and servants.
shortened: The Truth has, in most of His Tablets, commanded His maidservants and servants to perform praiseworthy deeds, for through goodly acts and pleasing conduct has the Cause of God been and continues to be made manifest among His servants.

order.why: Keep the relation of accepted deeds and teaching.
Join assistance and the revelation of one’s station.
Retain the reported counsel to let conduct guide others.
Imagine practiced teaching as a magnet.
shortened: Today the magnet of existence is conduct according to the divine teachings.

order.why: Read the reported effect of conduct in attracting or repelling people.
shortened: "Therefore, it is now proven that we are ourselves the means of our degradation and exaltation; that the people are attracted to us or repelled by us according to the attributes and deeds emanating from us.

order.why: Preserve the extended banquet imagery as an invitation to visible action.
Keep the particular address to believing women.
Retain the source’s special praise of believing women’s acts.
shortened: One deed performed by believing handmaidens takes precedence over the deeds of all the handmaidens of the earth.

order.why: Read the named friends and the call to sunlike purity.
shortened: Today the deeds of the friends of the Self-Sufficing, the Exalted, distinguish them from the people of the earth. O My loved ones! Hold fast unto sanctity and detachment. Your deeds must be so holy and pure that they will be even as the sun amidst the works of creation.

order.why: Keep the stated standard of honor and elevation of the Word.
Preserve the brief appreciation of deeds already accomplished.
shortened: In this transient world no matter continues permanently. Sometimes there is dismissal and sometimes appointment, sometimes there is success and sometimes lack of joy. What matters are deeds and actions, and praise be to God, those are in utmost perfection.

order.why: Consider the remembrance given to one pleasing deed.
Keep the particular matter of funds and deeds opening their own door.
shortened: Concerning what was mentioned about the matter of funds and the sons of the Two Lights lacking knowledge thereof - pure deeds reveal themselves and open their own door.

subjects.displayTitle: Christ’s suffering and rejection: recognition, humility, and forgiving love
subjects.introduction: He had no throne, not even a mat; no sword, not even a staff. Those who had prayed for the Messiah every night for fifteen centuries looked at the man from Nazareth, measured Him against David’s throne and the rod of iron, and called Him a false Christ. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells the story again and again, not to shame a people but to unsettle anyone who is sure of what the Promised One must look like. Fishermen recognised what the Sanhedrin could not; the crown of thorns of His lifetime became, on millions of later images, a crown of gold. At the centre stands the prayer from the cross for those who did not know what they were doing, which ‘Abdu’l-Bahá names as the whole purpose of Christ’s suffering: that love might shine in human hearts. The same pattern, He warns, met Muhammad and the Báb, and waits for Christians who adore an imagined church. To follow it further is to look at the crucifixion itself, at Judas and the trembling of Peter, and at the literal interpretation that turns scripture from a door into a wall.
subjects.arc: Begin with forgiving love and the purpose of sacrifice; examine the gap between expectation and recognition; explore rank, interpretation, suffering and the disciples’ trials; return through later remembrance to reconciliation and lived fidelity.

order.why: Read sacrifice through the aim of love and the hope of overcoming misunderstanding.
shortened: Let us consider His Holiness Jesus Christ: how many trials he accepted along this pathway, how many difficulties and persecutions, even giving up his life. He chose for himself the cross, so that the light of love might shine in the hearts of men, and the various contending nations come into a state of affinity and love, so that love might encompass the hearts of humanity.

Contrast the crown of thorns with later crowns of gold.

At the same time another man was praying and asking forgiveness of GOD. Christ said that the Pharisee's praying was not accepted in the Kingdom of GOD, but the prayer of the poor man was accepted.

Question the ease of later profession after a revelation’s setting.

But when He came, they were deprived [of Him]; indeed, they rejected Him, saying, "This is not the true Messiah!"

order.why: Keep the separate reported account of eager expectation and failed recognition.
Retain the public address’s question about expectation and rejection.
Read the argument for investigation in its public-address setting.
Retain the reported argument for investigation with its historical claims.
Consider the role attributed to inherited interpretation.

shortened: In the Bible there are prophecies of the coming of Christ. The Jews still await the coming of the Messiah, and pray to God day and night to hasten His advent.
When Christ came they denounced and slew Him, saying: “This is not the One for whom we wait.

order.why: Preserve the extended reported portrait of anticipation and opposition.
shortened: The Jews for a thousand and five hundred years were awaiting the coming, and their utmost desire was to live in the day of the Messiah.

Every night they slept with the hope that in the morning Christ would come, and every calamity which befell them, they were comforted in the thought of the coming of Christ. Nevertheless, when Christ manifested Himself, all of them denied Him. They became haughty and opposed Him; they applied to Him the term of Christ the liar, or, the false Christ; and they arose to kill Him. The very ones who so eagerly awaited His Manifestation made the thorny crown and placed it on His holy head; mocked Him; degraded Him in every way, and finally crucified Him.

order.why: Retain the reported series of questions about neglected forms of evidence.
shortened: For one thousand and five hundred years the Jews prayed and expected the coming of their Messiah, yet when He appeared amongst them with His beautiful Countenance and spiritual laws, what causes induced them to refuse Him and what reasons brought about their deprivation? Why did they negate him, notwithstanding the presence of creational proofs, tangible proofs, emotional proofs, inspirational proofs, intellectual proofs, philosophic proofs and scriptural proofs? Why were they not quickened by the Messianic breaths? Why did they not partake of the sanctifying graces of the Holy Spirit? Why did they arise against him and cried out crucify him crucify him?

order.why: Read the letter’s account of expectation, denial and the Gospel epithet.
Keep the particular catalogue of expectations in its theological argument.
Preserve the concise reflection on waiting and veiling.
Read the personal counsel about recognition and heedlessness.
Keep the address to an expectant household and its dawn imagery.
shortened: Convey my greeting and praise to thy respected husband and say to him that the Jews are still expecting Christ and long to see Him in all anticipation and great zeal, while His light was manifested, His beauty shone forth, His call was raised, His trumpet blown, His standard hoisted, and His stars sparkled; but the Pharisees are yet in an amazing slumber, immersed in former traditions, and they make play with the signs of Thy Lord, the Merciful, the Clement.

Preserve this source’s interrupted question concerning authority.

shortened: O thou who art honorable and faithful to God!

How many men and women awaited the manifestation of the Messiah after Moses? Yet when His beauty shone forth and His face appeared, they (the people) did not recognize Him, but continued to follow the superstitions of the Pharisees, who used to say: "Where is the authority of the Messiah?

order.why: Read the call to reflect on doubts and lost opportunity.
shortened: Look to the time of Christ and how they objected to that radiant countenance and denied Him because of doubts that overcame their hearts, and deprived themselves of that mighty grace.

order.why: Widen reflection toward the veiling of successive communities.
shortened: However, when the shrill voice of the Most Exalted Pen was raised between earth and heaven and the Countenance of the Manifestation appeared manifest and resplendent from the horizon of divine will, all became occupied with their own vain imaginings and turned away from the Sun of Truth, save whom God willed. And fewer still reflected on what caused the Jews to remain in expectation until this day, or what led to the veiling of the Christians.

order.why: Keep the brief comparison concerning continued expectation.
Retain the appeal to certitude against imagined expectations.
shortened: Yet those souls who throughout ages and centuries awaited the appearance of Him Who conversed on Sinai are today veiled and deprived of the ocean of grace. They have abandoned the Book of Certitude and cling to vain imaginings.

order.why: Read the concise paradox of denying the One previously invoked.
Preserve the source’s retrospective judgment as its own claim.
Keep the contrast between long entreaty and the grief of revelation.
shortened: Throughout ages and centuries they beseeched and implored from God, glorified be His majesty, to attain the presence of this Day, yet when the horizon of the heaven of Revelation was illumined by Him Who conversed with the Sinai, they did that which caused the eyes of grandeur to weep and the trees of the most exalted Paradise to lament.

order.why: Read devotional reputation alongside the preference for ornaments and suspicions.
Ask how an intended means of approach can become an obstacle.
shortened: Consider how most of the Jews in the time of Christ were occupied day and night in their places of worship reciting the Torah, yet these very acts prevented them from recognizing the Dayspring of the Cause of the All-Glorious, for all deeds are meant for attaining unto God and His good-pleasure.

order.why: Distinguish attachment to a name from attention to virtues.
Explore the sun and its changing place of appearance.
Keep the reported contrast of loving light and fixing on a dawning point.

Read the public address’s application of that metaphor.
Keep the reported continuity of light between Moses and Christ.
shortened: Thus, when Jesus Christ came the Jews could not believe that the same light which was in Moses was manifest in Christ.

order.why: Retain the reported argument connecting understanding Moses and recognizing Christ.
Read the letter’s account of Christ’s relation to Moses.
shortened: When His Holiness Christ appeared, they (the Jewish people) thought that holy personality intended to take away the eternal honor of Moses. Moses, in the eye of Israel, had no equal. Now, these had never thought that a greater than him (Moses) would appear. So this way of thinking became the cause of their being kept away from the Light of Christ and they were prevented from the precious things of the Holy Spirit, notwithstanding the fact that the greatest friend of Moses was Christ and He made His Holiness Moses great in the eye of the world and made Him to be glorious in the contingent world; whereas, even now, Israel (that is, the Jews) deny His Holiness, the promised Christ, and count Him to be an enemy of His Holiness Moses and of Aaron and David; and they were kept away from the bounties of Christ.

order.why: Keep the public address’s claim that Christ upheld Moses.
Preserve the reported argument against treating the two as enemies.
Consider the account of a Covenant extending beyond time.
shortened: Consider Moses, He Who conversed with God. Verily, upon Mount Sinai, Moses entered into a Covenant regarding the Messiah, with all those souls who would live in the day of the Messiah. And those souls, although they appeared many centuries after Moses, were nevertheless---so far as the Covenant, which is outside time, was concerned---present there with Moses. The Jews, however, were heedless of this and remembered it not, and thus they suffered a great and clear loss.

order.why: Retain the interrupted account of objections concerning enduring law and Sabbath.
Read the charges concerning law, Sabbath and Temple as the source reports them.
Keep the assertion that such accusations failed to halt the Gospel.
Read the reported expectation of extending an existing order.
Keep the reported list of expected external signs.
Explore the questions about origin, kingship and the rod of iron.

They said: "Christ come down from Heaven! We know that he was born of Mary; he has not a sword, not even a stick! He does not establish the throne of David. He comes in a desert: he has no home, and no food: he is a wanderer in the land. He has not even a mat."

order.why: Preserve the concise reported statement about symbolism.
Read the argument distinguishing reading from understanding.

And because they believed in revelation, that was the only veil that covered them (kept them from believing). As they were veiled from Christ, they did not understand the revelation of the Bible, but had they believed in the explanations given by Christ, and which were inspired, they would have understood the meanings of these prophesies.

Notwithstanding all this, in truth Christ did have sovereignty; but it was not earthly, it was heavenly.

order.why: Read the name of the Father through attributes and perfections.

They did not see that the prophecy was being fulfilled in Christ, because they were waiting for a great victorious material kingdom to be established on earth, and the Messiah was to be one who possessed endless wealth and sovereign earthly power; while Christ came in a contrary manner to this, and the Jews would only obey and accept according to their desire and the will of man.

order.why: Preserve the reported contrast of punitive kingship with light and life.

First: They were expecting him to come from an unknown place. They knew that His Holiness came from Nazareth. This is written in the Bible. They understood that His Holiness would have to come from an unknown place. This they learned from the Books of the Prophets not from their own imaginations.
For three years he lived under the greatest difficulties.

shortened: Likewise consider the appearance of Jesus, son of Mary. All the Pharisees among the Jewish clergy denounced that King of existence, and Annas, who was the most learned divine of that age, pronounced the death sentence against Him. Yet Peter, known as Simon, who was but a fisherman on the shores of the sea and had not learned a word of the outward sciences, accepted and believed in Him upon hearing but a single word from that Manifestation of the Divine Cause.

order.why: Retain the source’s contrast with tax collectors.
shortened: Annas and Caiaphas, who were among the learned of that age, pronounced the death sentence upon His most pure blood, while certain tax collectors were honored with the grace of faith.

order.why: Preserve the further separately sourced contrast.

shortened: Some thoughtless ones found these utterances of Christ strange, and even mocked them. How could this scattered band of paupers, rejected and spurned by all, ascend to the heights of eternal glory, become illumined and be the cause of enlightenment to East and West? How could a fisherman reach the height of the moon? How could a carpenter become the center of light?

order.why: Consider the listed positions of worldly power and privilege.

shortened: They were too entrenched in their sacerdotal authority and surrounded with the unlimited power of Sanhedrin. They reasoned that if they followed Christ, all these worldly pageantry and honor will be slipped out of their hands;- thus they incited the mob to cry: 'Crucify him! Crucify him!'

However thus much can be said: His Holiness Christ did not rest for one moment nor did he inhale one breath comfortably. He walked around these shores, through these mountains and across these plains. He had no refuge and no shelter, no home and not even a place to lay his head on.

order.why: Read the reported account of solitary travel and deprivation.

shortened: Consider that in the days of Christ, glory be to Him, no one gave importance to the guidance of the apostles. They said these were just some fishermen gathered around someone speaking words. Indeed they mocked, even laughing at Christ's blessed person Himself and spitting on that radiant, beautiful, sweet face.

order.why: Keep the source’s explanation of disrespect in its polemical vocabulary.

shortened: They considered that Light of Guidance as pitch darkness, and that Prince of Faithfulness as a terrible serpent of unfaithfulness. Even until now they loose their tongues in condemnation of Christ, and with unseemly countenance call that Beautiful and Comely Face "distorted." Yet in the market of the jewelers, that Brilliant Gem has the splendor of a Badakhshan ruby, and in the sight of those endued with insight, that Luminary of Truth displays the radiance of the brilliant sun.

order.why: Keep the cited rebuke and its claimed later manifestation.
shortened: Ponder thou these words of the Spirit Who, addressing the people, proclaimed: "O generation of vipers!" Today the mystery of those blessed words hath been made manifest, for after the appearance and descent of that Luminous Temple from the heaven of divine Will, all turned away from Him and clung to their own idle fancies, save such souls as were endowed with true hearing and true sight.

order.why: Retain the scriptural allusion concerning Mary within its argument.

shortened: I can only say what Thy servant Jesus - may my spirit be a sacrifice for Him - said when God said: "O Jesus Son of Mary! Didst thou say unto men, 'Take me and my mother for two gods beside God?'"

What hatred and persecution! How they scoffed at Him in derision and contempt! Consider the titles and epithets they bestowed upon His majesty! They even designated Him Beelzebub -- Satan. They put on His head a crown of thistles; nay, more, they cast dust in His face--into a face whereby the heaven and the earth is illuminated! They turned their backs upon Him, then bowed and said: "Peace be unto thee, O King of kings! Peace be unto thee, O King of the Jews!"

Read the reported continuing oppression during and after life.
Introduce testing even within the closest circle.

shortened: In that time no one but a certain few persons believed in Him; and the great one among them was Peter the disciple, who, through the burning of the fire of test and persecution, was in great fear and denied Christ three times; then the Jews who were scoffing persecuting, deriding and laughing at Him, despised Him as though He were a thief, a murderer, or a villain, and committed against Him that which made the hearts lament, distressed the minds, caused tears to flow and the foundations of existence to tremble and shake!

order.why: Let the Rock’s trembling make vulnerability tangible.
shortened: Peter, who was the Rock (of the Christian dispensation), was firm and solid; but, in the moment of Christis deliverance, that Rock quaked a little, until the crowing of the cock was raised.

order.why: Preserve the omission in the account of doubts and Judas.

order.why: Keep the reported use of Christ’s rejection to prepare believers for blame.

The Jews prove from the Bible that Jesus was a false prophet, so this is nothing new. It is always so. Let them go to the Rabbi and see what he will say about Jesus.

order.why: Keep the reported account of repeated persecution of Christians.

shortened: Jesus Christ--May my soul be a sacrifice to him--had only a few followers in the time of his departure. order.why: Keep the reported image of a few souls whose light spread.

order.why: Read steadfastness through the letter’s comparison with the apostles.

The result was that His lamp became ignited, His light began to shine and His followers sparkled like unto the stars from the horizon of existence; and the consequence to the Pharisees was the pangs of remorse and regrets."

Explore the reversal between intended abasement and later glory.

Keep the reflection on religious prominence and passing traces.
Preserve the source’s imperfectly punctuated comparison of reversed rank.
shortened: Remember the Day of Jesus, how many thousands of the Pharisees used to scoff at that glorious Lord: Then the necks of the Pharisees were humbled and their heads (made to bow to one of His maidservants, or one of His servants.

order.why: Read the Moses-garden imagery and the receptive few.
shortened: O thou flower of the garden of Christ! At the time when Christ (may my spirit be sacrificed for Him) with a radiant face and graceful beauty unveiled Himself and manifested His heavenly splendor among the Jews, Israel imagined that by virtue of the bounty of the rain of the All-Merciful that land was a rose garden, but it became evident and clear that it was a field of thorns, except for a few souls who, through the grace of the Holy Spirit, appeared like flowers in the utmost freshness and grace - these were the sweet flowers and fragrant herbs of Moses.

order.why: Keep the reported reflection on delayed acceptance.
shortened: "Look ye at the time of Christ - had the people realized that the Holy Spirit of GOD was speaking to them through His Divine Mouth, they would not have waited three centuries before accepting Him.

order.why: Retain the reported account of later recognition through the spread of faith.

shortened: His Holiness Christ manifested in these countries, but in the beginning His Cause was spread in Europe and it superseded all other religions, notwithstanding that in Asia there were many religions, such as Zoroastrianism, Judaism, the star-worshippers and idolaters, who are still existing in India. order.why: Keep the stated interval in the reported explanation.
shortened: At first, people did not accept Christ's Cause, but later when its intense radiance shone upon the kingdoms of hearts, then they understood. It took three hundred years for His Cause to spread in Europe.

order.why: Read the letter’s account of Helena and the rediscovered tomb as attributed.
shortened: For instance, consider the day of Christ, which was the day of the renewal of the Kingdom of God. The people of the world attached no importance to it and did not realize its significance to such an extent that the sepulchre of Christ remained lost and unknown for three hundred years, until the maidservant of God, Helen, the mother of Constantine arrived and discovered the sacred spot.

order.why: Retain the reported claims about burial and denial of Christ’s existence.
shortened: They gave so little importance to Christ that it is not even known where He was buried - such was their indifference.

It was considered so unimportant that one of the philosophers of that time who wrote a book against Christ says this person Christ never existed and there was no such person - Peter and Paul invented him.

order.why: Preserve the reported reflection on the absence of contemporary writing.
shortened: I was thinking that during the days of Christ not one word was written about him. We have at present time in our hands four Gospels, two of these were written 60 years after Christ; but today there are ever so many books written on the Cause, proving its authority and greatness.

order.why: Keep the letter’s contrast between initial mockery and later significance.
shortened: Consider that in the days of Christ (may my spirit be sacrificed for Him), they gave no importance to Christ's Cause, rather they mocked and ridiculed Him and according to the text of the Gospel called Him Beelzebub. Now observe what importance it later attained.

order.why: Read the Gospel’s worldwide light against its initially slight estimation.

Read the separate reported critique of listening to bells after neglecting the voice.
shortened: Christ Himself cried out, yet they gave no heed; rather, they showed Him the utmost contempt and humiliation. Now they install inanimate metal in His name and hearken endlessly to its sound, hastening toward it.

order.why: Keep the reported comparison with later pilgrimage to stones.
shortened: In the days of Christ He was despised, cursed and rejected, but after 1000 years people came from half around the world to visit some stones upon which tradition says He once sat. how much greater will these days be when they are once known.

order.why: Read the remembered scene of pilgrims at the lake.
shortened: His Holiness Christ spent most of His time on the shores of Lake Tiberius, but, alas, none of His sacred fragrances have remained. Sanctified is God! Near the lake's mineral waters, I saw the European pilgrims had prostrated themselves over the shore's pebbles and were kissing them, some weeping profusely.

order.why: Retain the separate reported encounter concerning a disciple’s stone.
shortened: In the desert, I found a number of Europeans collected and were kissing the stones, I said to them, "What means this kissing of stones?" They replied: " History tells us that one of the disciples of His Holiness, the Christ while travelling these parts sat on one of these stones.

order.why: Keep the reported contrast between a persecuted wanderer and later institutions.
Examine the reported comparison between Christ’s poverty and ecclesiastical luxury.
Turn the source’s critique toward later rulers who invoke a name.
Keep the reported question of sacrifice and continuing darkness.
Preserve the brief reported criticism of an interpretation of redemption.
Read the reported reflection on the Temple episode.
shortened: Christ went into the Temple of the Jews where He spoke on the teachings of the Torah prohibiting buying and selling in the house of God. Up to the present time Christians glory in this and rejoice over it.

order.why: Keep the separately reported interpretation of that episode.
Read the source’s quoted lament over unrecognized visitation and peace.
Consider the definition of a true religious guide through recognition.
shortened: This is not the day whereon the high priests can command and exercise their authority. In your Book it is stated that the high priests will, on that Day, lead men far astray, and will prevent them from drawing nigh unto Him. He indeed is a high priest who hath seen the light and hastened unto the way leading to the Beloved.

order.why: Retain the concise comparison across prophetic times.
shortened: Thus did the idolaters speak in the time of every Prophet until the days culminated in the Days of God and the Beauty of Eternity shone forth from the horizon of the Most Exalted Name.

order.why: Keep the reference to opposition to Moses.
Preserve the reported reminder of Moses and the calf.

For thirteen hundred years, ranks upon ranks of divines appeared and occupied themselves with mentioning and speaking of the Intended One from pulpits. order.why: Preserve the severe judgment of a sect as historical polemic.
Keep the source’s critique of presumed knowledge and the resulting judgment.

On the Day of Reckoning, the fruit of the deeds of those heedless souls was that they pronounced sentence against the Lord of all worlds and martyred Him.

order.why: Read the warning addressed to the people of the Bayan through the preceding example.

Yet when the Sun of Truth shed its radiance and the horizon of the world became illumined, they became like clouds that intervened and prevented its rays. Finally they issued the decree for His death, as you have all heard and seen.

order.why: Read the source’s comparison involving the family of the Messenger.

He sent unto the leaders of the people the angels of the Cause with an illuminating Book. They entered their presence with a mighty and glorious Tablet. Among them were those who turned away and took not the Tablet, and those who took it and looked upon it as one in a swoon, saying "These are but tales of the ancients." And among them were those who took the Tablet with one hand and gave it less attention than can be reckoned, then cast it upon the ground, being among those who showed arrogance toward God Who created and fashioned them.

order.why: Retain the charged comparison of claims limiting divine power.
Preserve the source’s rhetorical comparison concerning opposition.

order.why: Keep the sweeping comparative judgment attributed to its source.
Retain the original brief selection about return and rejected deeds.
Read reunion against the background of missed expectations.
shortened: How many were the divines and the learned and the jurisprudents who longed for the presence of God, yet after His manifestation remained deprived thereof, while thou didst drink from the choice wine of reunion and didst attain unto the kingdom of meeting.

order.why: Apply the warning about literal expectations to Christians as well.
shortened: There were explanations about how nations were veiled and clarification of the signs of the Day of Manifestation - that like the Jews, Christians too are afflicted with vain imaginings and imitations, such that they are still waiting for stars to fall from heaven, even though each star is many times larger than the earth.

order.why: Read the Gospel allusions concerning homeland and unexpected entrants.
shortened: In the Gospel it is said that all the prophets have been without honour in their own country and homeland. Indeed, such is the case. Christ hath likewise said that many shall come from the East and from the West and enter the kingdom of heaven, whilst the children of the kingdom shall forsake it.

order.why: Keep the reported criticism of exclusive religious claims identifiable.
Preserve the locally situated reported judgment concerning Tiberias.
Keep the reported conversation with Esmael and its charged rhetoric attributed.
Retain the reported Saul-and-Paul comparison without turning it into a collective verdict.
Preserve the reported hypothetical claim in its own historical setting.
Keep the reported account of persecution and its asserted explanation attributed, without adopting blame for victims.
Retain the reported claim concerning conversions and prophecy.
shortened: The Jews would not accept Christ, but, because they see their Bible prophecies literally fulfilled, they are becoming believers in great numbers.

order.why: Keep the particular reported conversation about teaching Christ’s station.
Preserve the brief reported statement of changed belief.
Read the reported affirmation of enduring reverence for Christ.
shortened: Consider with what knowledge His holiness Baha'u'llah hath favored the Baha'is, that if they are given the whole world they will not deny Christ.

Keep the reported account of Mary Magdalene’s activity with its historical claims.
Let the hope that eyes and ears will open direct attention toward future understanding.
Close with the lasting value of an act of love whose worth is not yet fully known.
shortened: The love that she hath shown you, its value is not known at present, but after departing from this transient world, its value will become known and evident in the divine Kingdom, and even in this mortal world its value shall appear in future. In the days of Christ, guidance had no importance whatever to the deniers; now consider how much importance it hath gained.
